steps.title: Read a sentence in two moves
body: Every short Arabic sentence here has the same shape: a topic, then a comment about it. There is no verb — Arabic has no present-tense "is".
So read in two moves: first find the topic (usually the word with الـ), then read the comment. الطَّقْسُ حَارٌّ — "the-weather / hot" = "the weather is hot."
The comment can be a describing word (حَارٌّ), a place (فِي الْبَيْتِ), or a pointed-at thing (هَذَا بَيْتِي).

steps.title: Twelve sentences
steps.intro: Read each one aloud, decide what the topic is, then reveal the meaning. Tap 🔊 to hear it.

steps.title: Comprehension
steps.prompt: Which sentence tells you about the weather?

steps.title: You read whole sentences
